newsitem.title: ANGOLA: U.N. chief off to Zaire crisis summit in Togo.
newsitem.headline: U.N. chief off to Zaire crisis summit in Togo.

text.p: U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan left for Togo on Tuesday to attend an African summit on the Zairean civil war, saying he hoped progress could be made towards ending the conflict at the meeting opening on Wednesday.

Annan told a news conference in the Angolan capital Luanda shortly before he left for Togo that he hoped a basis could be created to end the conflict between the rebels, led by Laurent Kabila, and President Mobutu Sese Seko's government.
"The Zairean government has insisted that a ceasefire take place before talks can begin, and Kabila has said that talks must proceed before there is a ceasefire," Annan said.
"I hope that in Lome we will find a basis for moving forward by perhaps having a ceasefire and talks begin simultaneously."
A top U.N. official travelling with Annan said he expected high-level talks in the Togolese capital Lome to start immediately.
"It will either be Kabila himself who will talk to some of Mobutu's people or it will be Kabila's top representatives who will meet with them," the official said.
Kabila's rebels have seized nearly a quarter of Zaire since they launched their campaign to topple the ailing Mobutu in October.
In Kinshasa, a senior official of Mobutu's party said it was ready to share power with the rebels ahead of elections.
"We shall meet and after dialogue we will share power," Banza Mukalayi, vice-chairman of Mobutu's MPR party, told Reuters.
"First we will talk to find the mechanism for a ceasefire and then we will share power before elections," Banza said.
Mobutu and Kabila have sent teams to Lome for the special Organisation of African Unity (OAU) summit on the Zaire crisis starting on Wednesday.
Annan said if a ceasefire were agreed in Lome he would move quickly in sending a U.N. peacekeeping mission to the country.
"I would certainly like to get them there as quickly as possible if we get a ceasefire," Annan told Reuters.
"But the exact timing would depend on a number of things, including where the ceasefire lines are located."
Annan was in Angola for a four-day visit to jump-start the country's stalled peace progress.
